title: Bupe not dissolving under tongue.
body: So apparently bupe takes around 10mins to dissolve under the tongue right? for some reason mine just dont dissolve iv been sat now currently 25 mins with them under my tongue and they are still the same. any tips?
comment:
Bupe can take a lot longer depending on certain factors but for most people I've known it takes around 20-30 minutes to properly dissolve, and even longer for the drug to finish absorbing into the body (up to an hour without food or drink was recommended to us at the detox I went to).

Make sure you're not holding a lot of saliva in your mouth, as this can actually make absorption harder. If you haven't tried already OP, try crushing up your pill beforehand and then placing the powder under your tongue with the tongue pressed down to keep out as much excess saliva as possible. This is how it was administered to everyone at the detox I went to and you can also try taking half the dose at a time, so you're not overwhelmed with the amount under your tongue. Again, the less saliva you have is usually better, since too much can cause the pill to 'swish' around the mouth or get swallowed and not properly absorbed.

So many people end up wasting so much of their pills, it sucks.

Either way, good luck OP!

title: I need some help with dosing
body:
A little backstory: I have extreme chronic pain, and where I live pain medicine is controlled and so there are no doctors who will prescribe me anything for pain, which is frustrating. 
Anyway, I found a guy who has been selling me percocets for the last 6 months and I have been taking about 6 a day, sometimes more depending on how bad my pain is. The guy who provided them doesn't have anymore at the moment and I am suffering from withdrawals. The guy gave me Suboxone and said it helps with withdrawals, but the thing is he said he has no idea how much or how often I should take them and because this is the first time I have heard of this stuff, I'm kind of afraid of taking them especially since I don't know how much to take or how often to take them. 

So my questions are, what's the starting dose of this stuff? How often should I take them? How do I ingest it, do I swallow them? I thought I read somewhere you put them under your tongue, is this true? He gave me 2mg and 8 mg pills. Is that too much or too little? How long after my last percocet dose should I take it? My last percocet dose was 18 hours ago and I feel awful, and it will only get worse, right?  
I'm so torn on what to do. On one hand I want this crappy feeling to go away now, but on the other hand I'm too afraid to take something foreign to me that has never been prescribed. 

Not only do I have lots of questions about Suboxone, but I'm also looking for support. I'm just really scared right now because I feel like I'm dying.
comment:
If you were taking 30mg of OC a day, I probably start with just the 2mg pill.
It's taken sublingually. Hold it under your tongue until it dissolves. I usually hold the liquid in my mouth for 10 min after it dissolves then swallow it. 
Wait an hour. If you're not feeling relief, take another mg or two. I don't think you will need over 4mg a day. 
You may need to redose in 12 hours. You'll eventually figure out what works for you.
You don't want to over do it because taking too much can make you sick. 
Sub has an extremely long half life.

title: Did Xanax help you with Suboxone withdrawal/severe anxiety and panic attacks during withdrawal?
body: Hi everyone. I am trying to stop using Suboxone, but I am severely scared bc the last time I just stopped I ended up in the hospital bc I had severe anxiety attacks that mimicked a heart attack even called an ambulance, and my blood pressure was extremely high, they gave me a shot of Ativan and sent me home with alprazolam and I felt okay. Now I'm at that point again on day 3 of no Suboxone and I cannot sleep bc I Jult awake out of my sleep having panic attacks and I have a constant feeling of impending doom. I want to 100% stop taking Suboxone. I already have bad anxiety without all of this and mental issues, depression etc. And I am a mother of 3. I can handle the body aches, and rls, and all that I can push threw that. It's my mental I am terrified of bc it ends up disabling me and it literally makes me feel like I am having full blown heart attack it is every symptom of a heart attack. So did Xanax help you mentally, and temporally during your withdrawal from Suboxone? I was taking I think 0.25 mg of xannax before bed every day that's it not over doing it. Also did anything else help you or do you have any advice? Like I said, I will push threw the pain of withdrawal, and the rls etc. I just need help with the extreme anxiety and severe panic attacks etc. Thank you.
comment: Benzos have a paradoxical effect on me when I take them during opiate withdrawal. I can take up to 16-18 mg of Xanax in a day and still be pacing and jonesing and full blown panicked, when under Normal circumstances 2 mg would’ve put me to sleep. It just feels like a straight jacket on my brain, and it disinhibits me in a bad way. Suicidal ideation is a huge symptom of mine for opiate withdrawal and the one time I tried to cold turkey heroin with just Xanax I ended up blacked out on the floor trying to cut my wrists with a broken glass. It can be dangerous for me at least. Right now I’m tapered on my suboxone down to 0.5 mg a day and it feels like there’s hardly any opiate love at all in my brain, the anxiety is overwhelming, I’m once again taking 10-12 mg a day and still stressed, still can’t sit still, still can’t eat.

title: Why do you really want to quit subs?
body:
I’m not judging nor being accusatory but why do you personally truly want to be off of Subs. At one point in time they were a lifesaver to stop the damage and cycle of addiction. Lately I’ve been stabilizing but here were some thoughts that have entered my mind on why I would like to eventually come off of them. 

* The other night I was just feeling “meh”. Not up , not down. I’m not used to not being able to manipulate my body to feel a certain way. Made me feel trapped. Kind of depressed. Then the next morning I woke up and went to work and was glad I was on them and couldn’t use. 

* What if I could just be off of them. Then I wouldn’t need to be on something every day. Then I remembered how I felt the other night and am convinced I would have used “something” to feel better.

* I miss the highs. How do I ever capture that overwhelming feeling of positivity, peace (at that moment) and sociable person. A life without highs? Fuck. 

* How am I supposed to deal with these social events coming up. I don’t know who I am without manipulating my personality before entering these situations. I feel helpless at times not being able to manipulate my feelings to cope with “x” scenario. 

* Where the fuck is my reward after a hard work day 

* I’m just normal on them. I’ve never been normal. How is this a good life to live ? Life seems to mundane. I can’t alter myself. This is strange. 

So these are reasons in my head (fleeting but I’m just being real) of why I can see myself getting off subs. Not to say I would go use again but on subs we are all kind of maxed out on what we can feel. I’m not used to that and haven’t been in over a decade. 

Anyone else help share some reasons why you truly want off of subs. Are all of you just wanting off to be off of taking a substance or can anyone relate to what I’ve felt above? 

Thanks.
comment:
1. I just knew I had to finally pull the band aid off. If I ran out of subs I would feel like I was chasing the dope man like I was still a fiend, literally no different and it was depressing.
2. The feeling of taking something and feeling like I just threw on armor and a sword and was ready for anything was gone and had been gone for a long time.
3. Pretty sure they crashed my endocrine system, could still get a boner and have a sex drive. But I literally just felt like shit with no energy and had no interest in the opposite sex. A chick would want to come over and I'd just beat off and go to sleep instead. Made my legs kick and made me jump out of my sleep, memory problems, headaches, vertigo. So I figure they're probably not good for brain health long term.
4. I know if I got sent to some island without subs or any drugs I would find a way to survive, I wouldn't lay there screaming for subs and dope. Therefore these things saving me the rest of my life from impending doom is just my imagination.
5. I haven't gotten high on opiates in years, but I'm taking something that's bad for me in the end so I don't do something else I don't even want to do. Subs became my drug of choice and I felt it was ridiculous.
6. Just overall mental health, spirituality, mental clarity, whatever you want to call it. I would be pissed all the time over stupid shit, and would literally be yelling at people in my head like a lunatic on a daily basis. I hardly had a real belly laugh in years and just felt overall dread majority of the time with no connection to the people around me. Worked on stuff for years, tried to work on me and it was just process of elimination in the end.

comment: I was on Suboxone for over 10 years, and after not getting high for 6 I felt like it was time to get off them. I didn't taper low enough and it was a rough one, but one I was off them for a little bit I started noticing improvements. The dopamine started flowing again so music sounded good, food tasted great, my mind was sharper, and I had those highs that you don't get on Suboxone. After about 5 months I was feeling pretty good, the post acute stuff had faded, and I was super happy to not be in the cycle of taking Subs especially because they work so erratically for me. But then I started relapsing because the cravings came back and I knew I could get high without any buprenorphine in my system. It started out with kratom, then H, and finally I found fentanyl. I overdosed off four small rips of fentanyl and I'm lucky to be alive, or not have brain damage. The next few months I'd relapse, go on Subs and get clean, then repeat the whole process. Right now I'm coming off Suboxone for my third time this year. The good thing is I haven't let myself build up a really big physical dependency, but the bad thing is I haven't been able to stay clean, even though my relapses are weeks and sometimes months apart from each other. Being off Suboxone made me realize that I'm much happier without it though. I slept better, I had good dreams, my testosterone levels went back to normal, I had more energy, and I just felt better. Opiates disrupt so many functions your body depends on to feel good, so you'll feel better off them with time. But if you're at risk for relapsing or just don't want to go through the process of getting off them, which can be really hard, then there's no shame in taking them as long as you feel you need to.

title: Using pain killers to get off suboxone?
body: So. This is going to sound weird, but I actually wasn’t put on suboxone for opiate dependence. I was put on it 3 years ago because this new age doctor said it could help with my depression by raising my dopamine levels. Anyways long story short. 3 years later I am on testosterone therapy at 28. Because the suboxone killed my T levels so much. My libido/mood/energy/etc is still super up or down even with testosterone therapy. My hormone doctor says that getting off the suboxone would help immensely in making the testosterone work better. I want to get off the suboxone but I heard it’s worse then opiate withdrawals. Which I have no idea what those are like, but I have heard they are miserable. title: Snorting Subs Question/Experience
body:
So I know this has already been answered, yes you can snort suboxone, but that's not my question. Let me just say that I am not prescribed it and am not an addict, I simply just wanted to experience the recreational aspect of subs, as i dont want to try the actual drug, with subs being used to basically ween the user off, as far as i know. I used to snort Percocet 10mg pills and was spending close to 400 a month on them, but then just stopped one day, no withdrawal or anything. Recently I snorted about 25 Vicodens over the course of 5 days, they made me more tired and eventually once they wore off I got really nauseous and didn't wanna move, but I feel fine after I sleep. 

So anyway, I've done subs once, like 6 months ago. I was told by my friend that they are much stronger than percocet, and that a little piece crushed up should be good for me. So when I got home, I took a knife and cut off not even a quarter of the pill, probably idk, 1/12th or something, like the size of a grain of rice, crushed it up, and railed it. I don't remember a lot from the high but the weird part I am here to question is, I went to lay down as I was tired. However, soon after I kinda fell asleep but wasn't actually sleeping? I specifically remember my eyes being half open and me being aware I was awake, but also in a position like I was sleeping and I didn't move for like 3 hours. 

I was wondering if this is a bad effect or maybe I did too much at once? I was looking for an effect similar to percocet which used to give me a really calm feeling but also a super focused head high, followed by eventually passing out from being tired, similar to how I felt when I was taking oxycodone when I was in the hospital with cancer.
comment:
Yes. The place between awake and sleep. Perfectly restful, even slightly aware of it. Like watching a TV that is your dreams. Almost like your just watching and not in control. Closest thing to lucid dream and I’ve ever experienced…. 

But ya. Dope makes me so that. And subs make me nod too. Just not as euphoric. But still enjoyable

IME just tapering the suboxone is a much better way to go about this.
There is no way to get out 100% wd free.

Thanks in advance for all of your help! 🖤

I just started taking subs this past week. I secretly have had an addiction for 6+ years. I don’t want anyone to know I am taking the subs, but I don’t know where I should put them. 

Does anyone have any suggestions on good hiding places or items?!? 
I have my car, my purse, my dresser, etc… However, when I was using pills, I had a small pill case that didn’t look like a pill case, it kind of looked like a makeup compact. The strips are too big for that. 

Does anyone know of any stealthy items to hide the strips?

Also, am I not supposed to swallow my spit when the strip is in my mouth? How long?

What tips/tricks/advice do you have for someone who is Suboxone naïve?

I would also like to add, I am so happy that I found this drug to get me off of opiates. It is literally transforming my entire life! I plan to taper off within hopefully 3 to 6 months. However, I’m trying to give myself grace and told myself it might take up to a year. I just wanna make sure I never go back to pills again.

Thanks in advance for all of your help! 🖤

title: Using pain killers to get off suboxone?
body: So. This is going to sound weird, but I actually wasn’t put on suboxone for opiate dependence. I was put on it 3 years ago because this new age doctor said it could help with my depression by raising my dopamine levels. Anyways long story short. 3 years later I am on testosterone therapy at 28. Because the suboxone killed my T levels so much. My libido/mood/energy/etc is still super up or down even with testosterone therapy. My hormone doctor says that getting off the suboxone would help immensely in making the testosterone work better. I want to get off the suboxone but I heard it’s worse then opiate withdrawals. Which I have no idea what those are like, but I have heard they are miserable. And I have also heard suboxone withdrawals last longer. I guess my question is, could I stop the suboxone for maybe 3 days. Switch to maybe something like Percocet or Vicodin. Stay on those for maybe 2 months. And by the time the 2 months has passed the suboxone should be totally out of my system and then just stop the painkillers? I know this sounds crazy and stupid. But just wondering if it’s an option. I feel trapped on this drug. I just feel numb to life at times and I honestly feel like I felt better before I went on it. Thanks for any help. I heard reddit is a pretty good place for opioid help!

title: Day 23 update - please read if you're wanting to get off
body:
~preface~

Abused oxy for 2.5 years, started with small amounts but towards the end of it was using 200-300 mg most days. Then got on subs for 4 months. Tapered from 8 mg to 0.5ish. I felt good starting subs, and the taper was easy enough for the first couple months. Then the last month, under 1mg, I found myself hating the negative side effects and was just ready to be sober. I read so so so much about the withdrawals and stuff that I was really scared to jump. But at the same time I was just always in a bad mood, no energy, sex drive, feelings. I couldn't take being on subs anymore. So I got my affairs in order, told my dr, took a week off work, went out of town so I wasn't tempted and just fucking jumped. 

the jump & honeymoon phase~

The first few days following my jump, I constantly felt like it was right about hit me. That at any moment the real opiate wds were about to start. Body temp regulation was a bit off, mild RLS at night, insomnia - but nothing terrible at this point. After another few days of laziness I realized it wasn't going to fuck my shit up like I thought it would. In fact, I started feeling better!.  Got goosebumps from books, vibed to music, and cried from movies. Reached out to old friends I hadn't talked to in a while. My appetite came back with a vengeance. FOOD IS SO GOOD AGAIN. Suffer knowing the end is near and life will be soso much improved should help get through the tough parts. I ate like a beast. I can concentrate on things relatively easy. Sex is sex again.

~paws~

The mild withdrawals lasted about a week. Despite them I felt damn good having feelings and energy again even without getting much sleep. Then that chapter ended and a new one began. This one was different, I felt no physical withdrawals but the mental component was a struggle. Depression, lethargy, a bit anxiety - but still better than when I was on 0.5g subs. This was worst around day 10. However day by day, I began slowly building myself back up. Starting running, and noticed I felt much better after doing exercise. Kept eating healthy and taking care of my body. Kept staying busy with books and movies. Each day has been better and better. I'm now at day 23 and feel more like my old self than ever before. Still struggling a bit with sleep and energy but overall feel good and proud of myself for NOT being dependent on any god damn substance or medicine to feel okay for the first time in years. Totally worth it

To anyone fretting about jumping - 

I can't promise you that your experience will be like mine. Everyone is different, and that especially applies to sub metabolism. But please, please, please just trust yourself, your doctor's, and your loved ones that support you. Don't believe all the horror stories from reddit. It'll be over before you realize it. And it always does get better!!!!!
comment:

title: Day 23 update - please read if you're wanting to get off
body:
~preface~

Abused oxy for 2.5 years, started with small amounts but towards the end of it was using 200-300 mg most days. Then got on subs for 4 months. Tapered from 8 mg to 0.5ish. I felt good starting subs, and the taper was easy enough for the first couple months. Then the last month, under 1mg, I found myself hating the negative side effects and was just ready to be sober. I read so so so much about the withdrawals and stuff that I was really scared to jump. But at the same time I was just always in a bad mood, no energy, sex drive, feelings. I couldn't take being on subs anymore. So I got my affairs in order, told my dr, took a week off work, went out of town so I wasn't tempted and just fucking jumped. 

the jump & honeymoon phase~

The first few days following my jump, I constantly felt like it was right about hit me. That at any moment the real opiate wds were about to start. Body temp regulation was a bit off, mild RLS at night, insomnia - but nothing terrible at this point. After another few days of laziness I realized it wasn't going to fuck my shit up like I thought it would. In fact, I started feeling better!.  Got goosebumps from books, vibed to music, and cried from movies. Reached out to old friends I hadn't talked to in a while. My appetite came back with a vengeance. FOOD IS SO GOOD AGAIN. Suffer knowing the end is near and life will be soso much improved should help get through the tough parts. I ate like a beast. I can concentrate on things relatively easy. Sex is sex again.

~paws~

The mild withdrawals lasted about a week. Despite them I felt damn good having feelings and energy again even without getting much sleep. Then that chapter ended and a new one began. This one was different, I felt no physical withdrawals but the mental component was a struggle. Depression, lethargy, a bit anxiety - but still better than when I was on 0.5g subs. This was worst around day 10. However day by day, I began slowly building myself back up. Starting running, and noticed I felt much better after doing exercise. Kept eating healthy and taking care of my body. Kept staying busy with books and movies. Each day has been better and better. I'm now at day 23 and feel more like my old self than ever before. Still struggling a bit with sleep and energy but overall feel good and proud of myself for NOT being dependent on any god damn substance or medicine to feel okay for the first time in years. Totally worth it

To anyone fretting about jumping - 

I can't promise you that your experience will be like mine. Everyone is different, and that especially applies to sub metabolism. But please, please, please just trust yourself, your doctor's, and your loved ones that support you. Don't believe all the horror stories from reddit. It'll be over before you realize it. And it always does get better!!!!!

I am about to switch to Subs from H. I was taking 1.5g of H daily and was prescribed 16mg subs daily. 

I’m worried about PWD and an planning on waiting as long as possible into WDs before taking my first dose of Subs. I’ve read 26 on COWS scale is safe and will hopefully wait 48 hours + until starting. 

For my first dose, I would like to take 2mg and then take another .5mg every 2 hours until I feel okay. I am doing this to avoid having to take a full 16mg. 

I also plan on reducing the amount of Subs I am taking every 5 days by 25% until I am down to about .25mg and will then jump. If at any point I don’t adjust to a lower dose, I will increase by .25 and stay for another 4 days until I feel good. 

Any advise with any of the above? All opinions are appreciated.

comment:
If any of your H was cut with fentanyl then you're looking at a longer time between last use of it and then starting suboxone. Obviously hold out for as long as you can mentally, but know that inducing subs too early and triggering precipitated withdrawal will make you feel 1000 times worse. Pure hell on earth. 

Once you've waited enough time and want to start just start with ~0.5mg just so if there are still opiates on your brain's receptors then the PWD won't be too to bad. After an hour of your first dose you don't feel any relief or PWD then you can start increasing doses ~1-2mg at a time. You can always take more, not less. 

Buprenorphine doesn't get an opioid dependent user high but it's still one of the strongest opioids out there. 
If you're not careful it will cause a lot of harm. Stay safe!

comment:
I have so many comments to make, but I gotta go to work...

1. Don't snort zubsolv!! Thr naloxone is way more bioavailable up the nose. Naloxone can't be absorbed sublingually. That's why the films and tablets are all sublingual. If swallowed, you can get a little bit of naloxone through the stomach. 

Snorted = way more naloxone in the blood stream.  That's why they have a narcan nasal spray.

Narcan = shot or nasal spray.

So, soaking a suboxone strip and shooting it, or crushing and sniffing a tablet with naloxone in it = narcan'ing yourself.

Stick with sublingual, that way you get your meds into your system and NOT the narcan.

2. The dosing strength on zubsolv is a different number because it's a different compound. The zubsolv 5.7 has the same amount of buprenorphine as an 8-2mg suboxone strip.

Zubsolv comes in a wider variety of strengths because it was designed with a taper in mind. There are more steps in the taper because it's way harder to cut tablets than the strips.

3. Subutex isn't available in the US anymore. There is a generic version, that's just a buprenorphine only sublingual tablet. No naloxone.

The recommendation is that it's only for pregnant or breastfeeding women. It's getting harder and harder to write for it, so many pharmacies giving us hassles and shit.

It's going to continue to get harder to get. 

The only reason it exists for pregnant women is to create a failsafe in the case of abuse (sniffing or shooting).  The naloxone that becomes bioavailable when you snort or inject it = instant withdrawal.   Someone dependent on opioids who goes into immediate withdrawal, could jeopardize a fetus. The stress of withdrawal could kill a baby. 

So, they allow pregnant women access to the version without naloxone, so just in case, if a pg women decides to crush and snort or soak and shoot her meds (instead of taking "as directed"), the baby won't be at risk. 

4. The generic suboxone strips are not cheaper for everyone. Where I live and work, most insurance companies have made deals with indivior and suboxone the brand is the covered formulary choice, thus the generic strips are not covered and are costing way more.

Editing every single script to say "DAW brand name suboxone" has been a giant pain in thr ass.

It's so fucked up that these insurance companies and the pharmaceutical companies are making so much money off us, and making everything so fucking difficult and complicated. Ugh.

5. Some people looooove suboxone. Some people swear that zubsolv is the best. Some people do the generic bup-nal tablets and say they're great.

Everyone is different. Every single human has such a variety in metabolic factors.... It's so impossible to know if you'd respond to a med the same way as anyone else.

We do genetic testing to help shed light on a lot of metabolic factors that affect how you absorb / respond to substances.  Humans are so fucking different, there is so much variety, it's a miracle to me that any product exists for mass consumption. We all respond to substances soooo differently.

Most people who switch from one version of a bup-nal to another, do just fine. Some people have an adjustment period of a few weeks.

Just make sure you're taking whatever version you're on, as directed, to try and maximize your buprenorphine absorption.

There are a ton of tips on reddit about like drying your mouth out and not swallowing your spit, etc. You want as much to get absorbed sublingually, as possible. 

6. Good luck, op and everyone else on meds!!!

comment:
Hi. Long term lurker and have switched from Suboxone strips to Zubsolv to the old orange tablets then back to Zubsolv so I thought I'd pitch in my experience. 

I've been on Zubsolv 2 x 5.7/1.4 since getting out of rehab in 2016. In there it was all brand Suboxone strips. Zubsolv is supposed to have better absorption so 5.7/1.4 = 8/2 Suboxone. A guy in rehab told me about them. When I got out I decided not to taper and stay on bupe long term - maybe not forever but for a good long while. Why is another story. 

I don't remember if the doc wanted me to take Zubsolv or if it was the insurance company. Anyway, when the Suboxone strips rehab gave me on exit ran out, I switched to the  Zubsolv, and to be honest never noticed any difference. 

I was recently in the hospital for 15 days. Actually 2 different hospitals. I told them all the medications I am prescribed, including the Zubsolv. The first one put me on 10mg of Suboxone - an 8mg strip and a 2mg strip. I don't know how they arrived at that dose since 2 x 5.7/1.4 Zubsolv is supposed to be equal to 16mg of bupe. The dose reduction was not really a reduction because I only take 1 of those 5.7/1.4 Zubsolv a day. (My bupe doctor is over prescribing because of a clerical error on his part that he will not admit to. So, I have a nice amount set aside in case I ever get caught without a bupe doctor.)

When I got transfered, the second hospital gave me the old orange pills (still an 8mg and a 2mg). The 8mg orange tablets take forever to dissolve. I did get a mild headache the first day but that was it. When I got discharged, I went back to Zubsolv. Still never noticed any difference. 

I will mention that recovering from surgery while pretty much totally opiate blocked was an "interesting" experience. Even though I told them, and they were actively issuing 10mg of bupe per day, they still injected me with IV Fentanal and Dilaudid in pre-op (so they told me) and it had absolutely no effect. I asked the anesthesiologist if he used opiates in his drug regimen and he said yes. I said I hoped he had plenty of non-narcotic arrows in his quiver because I did not want to wake up in surgery (I didn't)!

That night, after surgery and post-op, back in my room, they injected morphine (don't know how much) and were giving me 2 x 10mg Percosette every 4 hours. Nothing. It was a long night. Kind of got off track but my point is, at least for me, switching from Suboxone to Zubsolv  to the orange tablets then back to Zubsolv never bothered me, other than a mild headache the first day they switched me to the orange tablets. I guess everyone is different. YMMV...

title: Doctor refusing to bump me up to 16mg suboxone
body:
Been taking Suboxone for about 2 years.  1 1/2 with this doctor.  Started off just buying them off the street to kick heroin.  Then went to a doctor and got a prescription.  Now I take 16mg daily even tho my prescription is only 8mgs because it just wasn't working the same.  I knew my doctor wouldn't let me go up to 16mgs so I just supplemented myself by buying them from people I know.  After about 6 months I got tired of buying them and just want to get them from my doctor but like I knew he refused.  Saying it's not your tolerance....  It's your emotions etc.  I call bullshit... My tolerance is definitely higher after taking it for 2 years.  

So I want to switch doctors.  Has anyone done this?  Any advice?  Do you think it will be easy to find a doctor that will actually give me 2 a day?  

Thanks
comment: I’m pretty sure your tolerance would only be that high because that’s what you were taking previously. And honestly most people would get used to 8 real quick, some not even feel it. This isn’t really a drug you want to attempt to take more of unless you don’t feel like you can stay sober on it. Especially after 2 years. But if you’re stuck on the idea most of the online places give 16mg right away. But just a warning, these telemed places have been causing a lot of problems and I definitely recommend you get a local doc. They might not be around much longer.

title: Tapering with liquid?
body: I see a lot of people who jump from very low numbers under .25 etc. I was wondering if it would be a good idea to take a 60ml bottle and dilute my strips into it and dose by drops. I'm prescribed 8mg but I'm down to 2-3mg a day. If it is effective, how can i measure it out per drop,?
comment:
I started doing this about 20 days ago.  What I did:

1.  Took 1 x 8mg pill, crushed to fine powder (I cant get strips, but they dissolve the same.)

2.  Tool a 30ml dropper bottle with a 1ml dropper with measurements printed on the dropper. (1 dropper = 1ml)

3.  Mixed 3:1 Propylene Glycol and distilled water for a total of 30+/- ml liquid mixture total.

4.  Mixed in the suboxone powder.  Shake vigorously.

4b. - optional.  I heat my finished solution either in a boiling water bath (microwave a coffee mug full of water for 2 minutes.  Remove from Microwave, drop sealed solution bottle in for 20-30 seconds,) or microwave the bottle itself for about 20 seconds, remove, shake vigorously. )

Doing the math of suboxone divided by total ml of liquid ( example: 8mg sub divided by 30ml = .26~.27mg per ml.)  I've dropped down to around .5mg a day, so roughly 2 droppers a day equals about .5mg a day.  

With this method you can slowly titrate by single drops at a time if you choose to.  You can always change the potency as well by using less than 30ml liquid, but I wouldn't recommend it. (Personal preference)

Hope this helps!

title: Hard to Wrap My Head Around
body:
I began MAT to assist with my stepping out of pain management with oxy/hydro after almost 11 years. As well, I needed to find a solution to address my chronic pain (Multiple Sclerosis/Broken Neck). 

I didn’t expect the pain relief to be as good as it is. My initial plan to stay in MAT for 90 days and then taper while searching out pain solutions. 

It’s now hitting home with me that Suboxone may be with me for a very long time as it works so well. I’m grateful, but I’m also anxious by the thought of being dependent, which we all know has or will happen (85 days on).

I wanted to stop the other drugs being prescribed by pain management because they weren’t working any longer and I was simply over the monthly hassle of going through the PM gauntlet. 

The MAT visits are so easy and simple and I don’t feel on guard all the time. But still, it’s hard for me to think/know Suboxone may be the rest of my life answer for me.

Anyone else using Subs for PM and experience anxiety about being dependent to keep your life moving forward?

I  think something that may be impacting my anxiety is that I’ve had the crap scared out of me by reading some Redditor’s posts about the hell they’ve experienced while tapering and let’s not forget the fear that sits under the surface of “What if I’m in a bad accident.”   

I’m not sure what it will take to decrease my anxiety surrounding Suboxone for life. All I know is I’m feeling tremendously better... pain is controlled, so I’m checked in and present. This is a lovely state to live in a compared to going to PM just to stay out of withdrawal. 

Pearls of wisdom anyone?
comment: Do what works for you. Your anxiety seems to stem from one or a few other's bad experiences. Remember that we are all different, and our reactions will be different, although similar in ways. IMO, Suboxone is a life-saving medication; it treats addiction and treats pain, depression, and anxiety in some of us. If it's working for you and you are comfortable with your treatment plan, don't let others influence you into making a decision that may not be the right path for you. I've been on Suboxone for five years now, and I don't fear being on Suboxone long-term or even the rest of my life. I fear what life would be like if it weren't an option. I hope that helps... Best wishes and hugs!

comment:
I've been on subs for pain management since 2009. It was my choice to switch to them over percocet.

I had some anxiety at first but here are some things that really lessened my anxiety. 

1) take only what you need. I take a bit less than I am prescribed and this reduced any negative side effects and allows me to keep an emergency stash of medication (this has grown over the years to be quite large lol). Dont ever tell your doctors this though. But now I feel like if an emergency happens I will at least have a good supply of my subs on hand.

2) find supplements or remedies that help with side effects. I use magnesium powder, metamucil, swiss kriss tablets and green tea to combat fatigue and constipation. 

3) talk to your doctor about your anxiety over what will happen if you were to get into an accident. From my personal experience fentanyl at high doses can overpower the suboxone enough for pain relief. I recently had a surgery while on subs and the fentanyl they gave me in my IV worked fine. They knew they had to give me enough to kill an elephant though due to the subs in my system. 

Suboxone had been a miracle for me as well. It works so much better than the pills and minimizes my addictive behavior that came with the pills. I like how they last forever and you don't have to have an empty stomach for them to work quickly like you do with pills. Anyways, feel free to ask me anything.  :)

comment: I also recently switched from long-acting oxycodone. I was taking a few pills more than prescribed here and there, so I finally decided to make a change before it got completely out of control. I was surprised at how well the subs control my pain. I was in terrible pain the first day while I was in withdrawal, but the subs started worked pretty well on my pain within the first day or two. Now that I’ve been on them a couple weeks, I feel that they control my pain as well as the oxy and there are many other benefits—like you said, the “pm gauntlet” I am happy to be rid of. My pm doctor wouldn’t let anyone pick up until day 31 ,so it was always a lot of fear and anxiety at the end of every month and I would usually be short the last couple days because I took extra. Plus the fact that they last so much longer! That was amazing to me and still is. I was on a long acting med and it still felt like it was a constant up and down, but now I feel very leveled off. I’m not sure what I’ll do in the long term. I can’t imagine taking these my whole life but I also hate being in pain. It’s comforting to hear that there are options if I have an accident or surgery.

title: Hard to Wrap My Head Around
body:
I began MAT to assist with my stepping out of pain management with oxy/hydro after almost 11 years. As well, I needed to find a solution to address my chronic pain (Multiple Sclerosis/Broken Neck). 

I didn’t expect the pain relief to be as good as it is. My initial plan to stay in MAT for 90 days and then taper while searching out pain solutions. 

It’s now hitting home with me that Suboxone may be with me for a very long time as it works so well. I’m grateful, but I’m also anxious by the thought of being dependent, which we all know has or will happen (85 days on).

I wanted to stop the other drugs being prescribed by pain management because they weren’t working any longer and I was simply over the monthly hassle of going through the PM gauntlet. 

The MAT visits are so easy and simple and I don’t feel on guard all the time. But still, it’s hard for me to think/know Suboxone may be the rest of my life answer for me.

Anyone else using Subs for PM and experience anxiety about being dependent to keep your life moving forward?

I  think something that may be impacting my anxiety is that I’ve had the crap scared out of me by reading some Redditor’s posts about the hell they’ve experienced while tapering and let’s not forget the fear that sits under the surface of “What if I’m in a bad accident.”   

I’m not sure what it will take to decrease my anxiety surrounding Suboxone for life. All I know is I’m feeling tremendously better... pain is controlled, so I’m checked in and present. This is a lovely state to live in a compared to going to PM just to stay out of withdrawal. 

Pearls of wisdom anyone?
comment: I don't think it will be easy but I refuse to believe it will be anything close to the hell I experienced coming off fent.  A slow taper is my plan and I will take what comes.  Fent WD was traumatizing.

title: How did you decide your last dose day?
body:
When tapering off Suboxone/Subutex how long did others stay on their lowest dose before stopping completely? I am down to approximately 0.175mg of subutex and wondering when to just stop taking it. I've only been on this dose for a week and had zero WD or any issues at all. 
I have been on suboxone/subutex maybe 5 or 6 years started at 16mg now at 0.175mg - a little less than half of a 0.4mg subutex tablet.  I tried volumetric dosing but wasn't for me. I take it sublingual.
comment: I’d start skipping days for a while. Then do every third day for a while. That way you’ll have an easier time jumping and you’ll also have a pretty good idea what you’ll be in for. The slower you go the easier time your body will have adjusting.

title: Joy, happiness, and freedom!
body: I sit here writing this with tears of joy in my eyes! I am officially at the 30 day point and feeling fantastic! I would not be where I am today if it were not for suboxone maintenance, but after 11 long years on it I am officially done! They saved my life years back and have allowed me now to start a beginning of a new life! In a couple months my husband and I will start a family which is my motivation and inspiration to stay sober! IF I CAN DO THIS ANYONE CAN! If off is what you want do not be scared! Taper down and jump off, it's not as horrible as all the horror stories you hear. Yes, even jumping at .5mg it still took a month to feel normal but the last 30 days went so so fast. I literally can not believe that I am here right now! It feels so good! I have such a special place in my heart for all us addicts! WE ARE THE STRONGEST PEOPLE OUT THERE! Thank you for all the support I have received through the subreddit! You guys rock!
comment: That is very reassuring to hear. Be sure to come back and update us. It gives me hope. Good luck!

title: Need a friend/advice.. anything!
body: This is a hard day for me. I’m in full withdrawal.. and I just want to die. I’ve been in recovery from pain pill addiction since 2017 with no relapses. I’ve been on suboxone since then. I recently moved to Seattle, WA and wanted to try and quit. I jumped at WAY too high of a dose and ended up in full withdrawal. I found a doctor here but I’m not making much money right now and I’m not going to be able to afford more visits right now. I work and have insurance but it doesn’t cover shit. And since I just moved I’m spending so much money on living expenses that I won’t have anything left for the appointment or medication. I’ve reached out to ALL the state sponsored programs but the waiting lists are ridiculous OR they won’t accept new patients that don’t test positive for opiates. So I’m scared.. I don’t know what to do. I’ve been crying on and off for 3 days, last night was complete misery. I didn’t sleep more than 5 mins at a time and had to get up and change my sweaty clothes 3 times. I’ve thought about getting kratom but I’ve read so many people here recommending against it. I don’t know what to do. I just want to be back on my medicine and feel better.
comment:
I am so sorry you going through it right now, I know how bad jumping from a high dose is. Have you considered looking into tele-health, lots of people on here talk about how cheap it is compared to in office visits. Second I know you said you have insurance have you considered contacting them and asking what places they may cover or how they can help? Also I wonder if  you would qualify for state assisted insurance or any kind of assistance to help so you would be able to afford it. Kratom can be expensive so IDK if that will be a good long term option. Maybe even consider looking into clinics in your area that may work on sliding scale for lower income people. It is complete bullshit to have and pay for insurance that doesn't help with what you need help with. I wish I knew more ways to help you and I hope you feel better ASAP. Try your best to eat and stay hydrated, take as many hot baths as you can, and try to relax as much as possible.

Edit: just want to add some tele-health to look into might be Bupe.me and QuickMD are the 2 I see most talked about. Some others might have other suggestions as well.

title: almost 30 days off subs! honestly- a near painless experience. i have v high anxiety, and this forum terrified me over the jump. do not let people trip you up! Lmk questions :)
body:
What nobody told me is pretty much 80% of the withdrawl happens under 1 mg. at < .5 doses, it is metabolized to such low levels, it only provides a few hours of relief. 

someone shared this with me over reddit, and I didn’t really believe them, but I noticed while the ends of the day were certainly a little more shitty (bad mood, fatigue) they were not bad at all or anything I would consider to be withdrawl. 

After reading that I thought I would give a shot at skipping days, as I supposedly already had I guess relatively small amounts of bupe in my system 

next thing I knew I accidentally went 4 days without any sub! 

took a tiny .15 mg dose, as i’m not in a hurry and wanted to land this plane smoothly as possible. after that last dose I noticed an upswing in my mood as soon as day 4. it’s gotten better every week since!

So fellas! land this plane! you wouldn’t crash it into the ground right? you wouldn’t speed up as you got closer to the runway, right? the closer you get to the finish line , the lighter you pull up on the “plane” and your efforts. 

same concept! your mental health is important to get through this successful. be nice to yourself. that’s the biggest issue I had.

Before volumetric dosing, I was having to cut up 8mg pills into 4 pieces of 2mg. Anything below that, and it got real difficult to cut up into accurate doses. Anything below 1mg and I wouldn't have been able to do it. 

Since dissolving my pills and using volumetric dosing, I've been able to bring my dosages down nice and slowly to make things as comfortable as possible. With me being a labourer, unless I'm at work, I don't get paid, so I really couldn't afford to take any extended periods of time off from work. Like most people, I've got bills to be paying. 

The plan is to continue dropping by 0.1mg every 10 to 14 days until I get all the way down to 0.1mg. After that, I plan on taking it slow until I get down to 0.025mg. After that, I plan on jumping. 

Hearing encouraging words like yours puts a smile on my face. Thanks to this subreddit, I've learnt a great deal. Without it, I wouldn't have known about comfort meds like Gabapentin and Clonidine either. 

Have you felt the need for comfort meds like Gabapentin or Clonidine? How's the anxiety? What about the shits? Have you been shitting your brains out? What about sleep? Are you still able to get a good nights sleep?

Thanks again and I'm really proud and pleased to hear things are going as smoothly as possible!

title: Taper vent
body:
Started my taper in March from 8mg, today I just went from 4mg to 3mg every other day (so today I’ll do 3mg, then tomorrow 4mg then repeat for about a week then go to 3mg every day). Honestly I’m very motivated so bring on the pain haha I just don’t care anymore I want off. 

Is anyone else really annoyed by having to cut up their subs into pieces? In the morning my hands literally shake while I’m cutting up the sub to the correct dose and I feel like even more of an addict lol. I finally asked for the 4mg strips from my doctor only to find out the 4mg strips are twice the size of the 8mg strips wtf (dr reddy generic brand). And now that I’m moving on to three it’s back to cutting them up and having all these little pieces to keep track of. Do you guys cut yours in advanced? I feel like even when I use scissors the strips are never even. This is mostly a vent because I have no one to really talk about this to that’s gets it IRL
comment:
Bigger strips are a GOOD thing if you're trying to cut them down. They're just like the 2s but double the size. Easier to get a smaller dose.

Corn starch on fingertips helps when handling strips. I crease between my fingers then cut with scissors, down to 1/8th of a strip. You could take a 4mg down to 1/16 squares which would be 0.25mg.

title: What an ironic cluster fuck.
body:
I've been on Suboxone for almost 6 years. Same doctor, same pharmacy, no problems. I have my first Sublocade shot on Monday and so I tapered from 8-4 with my last prescription. My doctor told me that if I needed to take 6 at first that would be okay and to let her know. I did and I did. I emailed her 11 days ago to let her know I would need my next prescription a few days early. I knew there would be an issue at WALGREENS so I emailed again to check in. Since yesterday I've had a phone appointment, a physical appointment, and numerous emails. The pharmacy sent my prescription somewhere else, then sent it back. They needed to speak with my doctor and now don't have any Suboxone in stock.  Today is the first time in almost 6 years I've had withdrawals. I know I should feel fortunate, but I just feel like shit. 

Any recommendations on comfort meds? I have muscle relaxers, some gabapentin I've never taken before, and a mild anti anxiety medicine my mom gave me. Does any of it actually help?

Edit- I've called my big brother. He might be able to help. Thank you to everyone that has offered information and advice. This sub means a lot to me. I appreciate you all so much..

Edit #2- my brother just left. I'll be ok until Monday. Thanks again ❤️
Peace & Love ❤️
comment: The gabapentin will help tremendously.  If your anti-anxiety med is a benzodiazepine it will ad to the gabapentin benefits. Dont take too much of the benzo- caution.

title: Taper vent
body:
Started my taper in March from 8mg, today I just went from 4mg to 3mg every other day (so today I’ll do 3mg, then tomorrow 4mg then repeat for about a week then go to 3mg every day). Honestly I’m very motivated so bring on the pain haha I just don’t care anymore I want off. 

Is anyone else really annoyed by having to cut up their subs into pieces? In the morning my hands literally shake while I’m cutting up the sub to the correct dose and I feel like even more of an addict lol. I finally asked for the 4mg strips from my doctor only to find out the 4mg strips are twice the size of the 8mg strips wtf (dr reddy generic brand). And now that I’m moving on to three it’s back to cutting them up and having all these little pieces to keep track of. Do you guys cut yours in advanced? I feel like even when I use scissors the strips are never even. This is mostly a vent because I have no one to really talk about this to that’s gets it IRL
comment: Yes, cut them up in advance. It's way too easy to take too much if you don't have a pre-cut dose handy. I hear consistently negative things about Dr. Reddy's so good luck with that. The size shouldn't be a problem though, right? Easier to make even strips with more to work with. You say you're very motivated so cutting the strips is a pretty minor nuisance compared to dealing with the effects of tapering.

span_if_claim:
To answer your questions: Yes, they can prescribe bup to a max of 30 patients a month (they may not know this)
Any prescriber with a DEA # (controlled substance prescribing abilities) can treat up to 30 patients a month per updated Federal Guidance released by SAMSHA late last year.
If a provider won’t prescribe a patient buprenorphine now, they are either ignorant to the new law or are lying (and to lazy to fill out one form)
Before the new rule, they had to do 8 hours on online modules and get a X# from the DEA to prescribe bup.
Now, they just have to submit a “Notice of Intent to prescribe buprenorphine” and they can immediately start treating up to 30 patients a month for OUD with bup.
No more online classes  if they stay under 30 patients a month.
If they go over, they will have to do the 8-hours and get “waivered” to prescribe more than 30 patients a month.
This is my understanding as it’s part of my job.
I may be wrong on some of the specifics.
These are still very new rule changes that were put into place by Trump and then followed through with by Biden before being implemented (crazy, I know)
Link for more info: [SAMSHA MAT](https://www.samhsa.gov/medication-assisted-treatment/become-buprenorphine-waivered-practitioner/new-practice-guidelines-faqs)

If a provider won’t prescribe a patient buprenorphine now, they are either ignorant to the new law or are lying (and to lazy to fill out one form)

Before the new rule, they had to do 8 hours on online modules and get a X# from the DEA to prescribe bup. 

Now, they just have to submit a “Notice of Intent to prescribe buprenorphine” and they can immediately start treating up to 30 patients a month for OUD with bup. No more online classes  if they stay under 30 patients a month. 

If they go over, they will have to do the 8-hours and get “waivered” to prescribe more than 30 patients a month.

This is my understanding as it’s part of my job. I may be wrong on some of the specifics. These are still very new rule changes that were put into place by Trump and then followed through with by Biden before being implemented (crazy, I know)

Link for more info: [SAMSHA MAT](https://www.samhsa.gov/medication-assisted-treatment/become-buprenorphine-waivered-practitioner/new-practice-guidelines-faqs)
